newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Exide and Tadiran in battery pact.
newsitem.headline: Exide and Tadiran in battery pact.

text.p: Israel's Tadiran Ltd said on Thursday it had signed a memorandum of understanding with the U.S. company Exide Corp to jointly develop and produce lithium batteries.
Tadiran chief executive officer Israel Zamir told Reuters that the terms of the agreement had not yet been set and it might include Exide's taking a stake in Tadiran's Tadiran Batteries unit.

"We signed a memorandum of understanding on cooperation and we are just on the start of the journey," said Zamir. "It's too early to know" where Exide would take a stake in the Tadiran Batteries, he said.
The agreement covers lithium metal and lithium ion batteries whose development has been pioneered by Tadiran, Zamir said.

In a statement, Tadiran said the two sides plan strategic cooperation in the segment that would combine Tadiran's technology and research and development capabilities with Exide's worldwide marketing organisation.
Exide, based in Bloomfield Hills, Michigan, is the leading maker of starting, lighting and ignition batteries and industrial lead acid batteries.

Tadiran said it had invested $20 million developing the batteries and another $10 million in building an automated production line capable of turning out about eight million of the batteries annually.
Lithium batteries, which are lightweight, powerful and have a lifespan of more than 10 years, are designed for use in cellular telephones, medical equipment and military hardware, Tadiran said.
Zamir said Tadiran had just begun sales of the lithium metal batteries and had recently completed development of the lithium ion battery.
